```{r results='hide', echo=FALSE}
#The following defines a convenience function for loading libraries, installing if necessary.
loadLibrary = function(packageName, suppressMessages = TRUE, githubRepo = NULL)
 {
  if (! require(packageName, character.only = TRUE)) {
    if (! is.null(githubRepo)) {
      loadLibrary("devtools")
      devtools::install_github(githubRepo)    
    }
    else 
      install.packages(packageName)
  
    if (suppressMessages)
      suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(packageName, character.only = TRUE))
    else 
      library(packageName, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}  
```

## Duration spent

```{r}
#how many participants? 
durationSummary<-  trialData %>% select(uid, sonaID, duration, credTime,confidenceTime,sharingTime, onlineResponseTime,commentTime) %>% group_by(uid, sonaID) %>% summarize(
  meanTrialDuration = mean(duration, trim=.25), 
  McredTime = mean(credTime, trim=.25), 
  MconfidenceTime = mean(confidenceTime, trim=.25),
  MsharingTime = mean(sharingTime, trim=.25),
  MonlineResponseTime = mean(onlineResponseTime, trim=.25),
  McommentTime = mean(commentTime, trim=.25)
  )

durationSummary
```

On average it seems to take 30 minutes per participant to complete the experiment.

```{r}
timeData <- trialData %>% select(uid, index,condition, mainHeadline, credTime, confidenceTime, sharingTime, onlineResponseTime, commentTime)

timeDataLong <-timeData %>% pivot_longer(cols = ends_with("Time"), names_to = 'TimeType', values_to = 'duration')

timeDataLong$TimeType <- factor(timeDataLong$TimeType, levels=c('credTime','confidenceTime','sharingTime','onlineResponseTime','commentTime'))
```

```{r}
ggplot(timeDataLong, aes(x=TimeType, y=duration)) + geom_boxplot() + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 30)) + ylab("Duration (Seconds)") + xlab("Trial question") 
```

```{r}
timeDataLong <- timeDataLong %>%
  group_by(condition, TimeType) %>%
  filter(duration > quantile(duration, 0.25) & duration < quantile(duration, 0.75))
```

```{r}
ggplot(timeDataLong, aes(x=TimeType, y=duration)) + geom_boxplot() + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 30)) + ylab("Duration (Seconds)") + xlab("Trial question") 
```

## Hypothesis and research questions

H1. Participants will give less corrective comments compared to reinforcing comments.

H2. Participants will be more discerning when giving corrective comments compared to reinforcing ones.

H3. Participants will be more confident in their credibility assessment

1.  a\. when giving comments compared to skipping.

2.  b\. when giving corrective comments compared to reinforcing.

## Analysis

#### H1 - Out of the corrective comments only a small proportion is given online compared to reinforcing comments.

People are more inclined to be skeptical of the headlines.

```{r}
table(data$percCredibility, data$onlineResponse)
```

```{r}
agg_data <- data %>%
  group_by(uid, percCredibility) %>%
  summarise(
    # Calculates the percentage of time each user chose to post the comment
    prop_post = mean(onlineResponse == "onlineYes", na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Reshape the data for a paired analysis
wide_data <- agg_data %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = uid, 
    names_from = percCredibility, 
    values_from = prop_post
  ) %>%
  # Drops participants who didn't encounter both tweet types to ensure valid pairing
  drop_na()

wide_data
```

```{r}
t.test(wide_data$percFalse, wide_data$percTrue, paired = TRUE)
```

```{r}
prop.test(table(data$percCredibility, data$onlineResponse))
```

```{r}
# 1. Ensure your binary outcome is read as a factor by R
data$onlineResponse <- as.factor(data$onlineResponse)

# 2. Fit the Multi-Level Binary Logistic Regression
# (1 | uid) controls for participant-level baseline posting tendencies
# (1 | index) controls for specific tweet-level variance
h1_model <- glmer(onlineResponse ~ percCredibility + (1 | uid) + (1 | index), 
                  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
                  data = data)

# 3. View the model summary and coefficients
summary(h1_model)
```

```{r}
# 4. Calculate estimated marginal means and run pairwise contrasts
# type = "response" converts log-odds back into interpretable probabilities
post_hoc_h1 <- emmeans(h1_model, pairwise ~ percCredibility, type = "response")

# 5. Display the detailed post-hoc results with corrected degrees of freedom
summary(post_hoc_h1)
```

```{r}
timeSummary <- data %>% select(percCredibility,onlineResponse, credTime) %>% group_by(percCredibility, onlineResponse) %>% summarise(mTime = mean(credTime), count = n(), sd=sd(credTime), se = sd/sqrt(count),ci = se * qt((1-0.05)/2 + .5, count-1))

timeSummary
```

```{r}
ggplot(timeSummary, aes(x=percCredibility, y=mTime, fill = onlineResponse)) + 
    geom_bar(position=position_dodge(), stat="identity", width = .7) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mTime-ci, ymax=mTime+ci),
                  width=.2,                    # Width of the error bars
                  position=position_dodge(.7)) + 
   ylab("Mean Duration") + xlab("Perceived credibility") + 
   theme_bw()  + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, vjust = 1, hjust=1))
```

```{r}
leveneTest(credTime ~ percCredibility * onlineResponse, data = data)
```

```{r}
cT.Aov <- aov(credTime ~ percCredibility * onlineResponse, data = data)
summary(cT.Aov)

TukeyHSD(cT.Aov)
```

There is no difference in time spent evaluating the credibility of the headlines where participants decided to comment online vs not.

#### H2 - Participants will be more discerning when giving corrective comments compared to reinforcing ones.

```{r}
data <- data %>% mutate(classification = ifelse( groundTruth == 'FALSE' & percCredibility == 'percFalse', 'hit', ifelse(groundTruth == 'FALSE' & percCredibility != 'percFalse', 'miss',ifelse(groundTruth == 'TRUE' & percCredibility == 'percTrue', 'hit','miss'))))

table(data$percCredibility, data$classification, data$onlineResponse)
```

```{r}

data$classification <- as.factor(data$classification)
data$onlineResponse <- as.factor(data$onlineResponse)
data$percCredibility <- as.factor(data$percCredibility)

h2_model <- glmer(classification ~ percCredibility * onlineResponse + (1 | uid) + (1 | index), 
                  family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
                  data = data)
summary(h2_model)
```

```{r}
post_hoc_h2 <- emmeans(h2_model, pairwise ~ percCredibility | onlineResponse, type = "response")

summary(post_hoc_h2)
```

```{r}
table(data$onlineResponse, data$classification)
```

```{r}
prop.test(table(data$onlineResponse, data$classification))
```

People are more discerning when it comes comments given online compared those that were not given.

```{r}
temp <- data %>% filter(onlineResponse == 'onlineYes')
table(temp$percCredibility, temp$classification)
```

```{r}
prop.test(table(temp$percCredibility, temp$classification))
```

miss proportion is less in corrective comments compared to affirmative comments in comments that were given online.

```{r}
temp <- data %>% filter(onlineResponse == 'onlineNo')
table(temp$percCredibility, temp$classification)
```

```{r}
prop.test(table(temp$percCredibility, temp$classification))
```

With regards to comments that were not given online, people were more accurate when identifying true claims compared to false ones.

```{r}
chisq.test(table(data$percCredibility)) 
```

This is because people are more cynical - tend to assume that headlines are false.

#### H3 Participants will be more confident in their credibility assessment

1.  a\. when giving comments compared to skipping.

2.  b\. when giving corrective comments compared to reinforcing.

```{r}
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(onlineResponse1 = ifelse(onlineResponse == 'onlineYes', 'Yes','No'))

data$classification <- as.character(data$classification)
data$classification <- paste0(toupper(substr(data$classification, 1, 1)), 
                              tolower(substr(data$classification, 2, nchar(data$classification))))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(commentType = ifelse(percCredibility == 'percTrue','Reinforcing','Corrective'))
```

```{r}
data$onlineResponse <- as.factor(data$onlineResponse)
data$percCredibility <- as.factor(data$percCredibility)

h3_model <- lmer(confidence ~ percCredibility * onlineResponse + (1 | uid) + (1 | index), 
                 data = data)


anova(h3_model)
```

```{r}
h3a_test <- emmeans(h3_model, pairwise ~ onlineResponse)
summary(h3a_test)
```

```{r}
h3b_test <- emmeans(h3_model, pairwise ~ percCredibility | onlineResponse)
summary(h3b_test)
```

```{r}

confSummary <- data %>% select(commentType,onlineResponse1, confidence) %>% group_by(commentType,onlineResponse1) %>% summarise(mConf = mean(confidence), count = n(), sd=sd(confidence), se = sd/sqrt(count),ci = se * qt((1-0.05)/2 + .5, count-1))

confSummary
```

```{r}
#png(filename = 'conf.png', units = 'in', height = 8, width = 10,res = 300)
ggplot(confSummary, aes(x=onlineResponse1, y=mConf, fill = commentType)) + 
    geom_bar(position=position_dodge(), stat="identity", width = .7) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mConf-ci, ymax=mConf+ci),
                  width=.2,                    # Width of the error bars
                  position=position_dodge(.7)) + 
   ylab("Mean Confidence") + xlab("Comment given online?") + scale_fill_discrete(name = "Comment type") + theme_minimal()  + theme(text = element_text(family = "Times New Roman", size = 20)) 

#dev.off()
```

```{r}
leveneTest(confidence ~ percCredibility * onlineResponse, data = data)
```

```{r}
rep.Aov <- aov(confidence ~ percCredibility * onlineResponse, data = data)
summary(rep.Aov)

TukeyHSD(rep.Aov)
```

```{r}
rep.Aov.residuals <- residuals( object = rep.Aov )
hist(rep.Aov.residuals)
```

```{r}
qqnorm( y = rep.Aov.residuals )
```

```{r}
shapiro.test(x= rep.Aov.residuals)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = interaction(percCredibility, onlineResponse), y = confidence)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Combination of Col1 and Col2", y = "Column 3")
```

```{r}
data$group <- interaction(data$percCredibility, data$onlineResponse)
t<- oneway.test(confidence ~ group, data = data, var.equal = FALSE)
t
```

```{r}
games_howell_test(data, confidence~group, detailed = TRUE)
```

- `.y.`: the y (outcome) variable used in the test.

- `group1,group2`: the compared groups in the pairwise tests.

- `n1,n2`: Sample counts.

- `estimate, conf.low, conf.high`: mean difference and its confidence intervals.

- `statistic`: Test statistic (t-value) used to compute the p-value.

- `df`: degrees of freedom calculated using Welch's correction.

- `p.adj`: adjusted p-value using Tukey's method.

- `method`: the statistical test used to compare groups.

- `p.adj.signif`: the significance level of p-values.
